final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mainly reframed the same record more narrowly. That narrower framing is materially better than claiming controls alone cure the issue, but it still does not satisfy the release condition on the present evidence. The admissible record supports that aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and rollout controls exist. It also supports that the affected public benefits eligibility segment remains exposed, the county gate does not exclude it, and there is no approved risk acceptance covering that exposure. Under the policy text, that means compliance requires admissible evidence of explicit pre-launch disclosure or approved risk acceptance. Because neither is in the record, this is not compliant_with_caveats; the caveat is itself an unresolved compliance predicate. The claim that certification is presently supportable remains insufficiently supported on admissible evidence alone.
remaining_concerns: There is still no admissible evidence that the required limitation disclosure was incorporated into the final launch artifact or model card before launch.
The affected public benefits eligibility segment remains below target and remains in scope for the initial rollout cohort.

The 7% county-based rollout, rollback switch, and monitoring are operational mitigations, but policy and record do not support treating them as a substitute for disclosure while the segment remains exposed.
The only risk-acceptance artifact is an incomplete draft with a blank approver line and no discussion of the public benefits eligibility exposure.
The actor's narrowed position is still conditional on an unresolved compliance predicate: explicit pre-launch disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
